title: Seen-set scale benchmarks before any post release: 10k/100k channel histories
description: Sol xhigh diff review (2026-08-22, finding 12): seen-state read cost is O(history) per read and every mutation rewrites the whole set. Ruling (coordinator): linear exact-state cost explicitly accepted for the interim; watermark+exceptions compaction is UNSAFE under the late-arrival model without a durable arrival-sequence fence (bigger feature, not this wave). Before any release: benchmark 10k and 100k message histories for state bytes, read/ack latency, watch CPU, memory; set thresholds; a write-time state-size warning ships separately.
close_reason: Ran on the Mac (release binary, generated valid envelopes, /tmp scratch root): 10k msgs -> state 400KiB, discard-all 0.18s, steady read 0.03s, single-ack 0.35s@100k/0.04s@10k, snapshot scan 0.03s; 100k msgs -> state 3.9MiB, discard-all 1.76s, steady read 0.31s, snapshot 0.33s. Linear exactly as the documented policy predicts; 10k is imperceptible, 100k (~30x any observed real channel) stays functional at ~350ms per op with the 50k write warning firing well before. Release-acceptable; no threshold breach; compaction remains deferred behind an arrival-sequence fence per policy.

title: Validating watch-notice renderer for native idle wake
description: Ship a small Node wrapper that turns post watch NDJSON into one bounded metadata-only notice line per batch. Grok monitor and Cursor background --once both wake on output/exit; raw watch NDJSON is not a safe injected payload (subjects/from are attacker-reachable).
design: skills/post/hooks/watch-notice.mjs. Spawn post watch with --once, --snapshot, or long-running (default). Pass through repeated --room. Validate every event with the same shapes as the lifecycle adapters. On a good non-empty batch, print exactly one line (Grok monitor treats each newline as a notification). Malformed batch: one UNKNOWN line, do not echo any event field. Scan failure: UNKNOWN on stdout, exit 1. Empty snapshot: no stdout, exit 0. No pgrep/pkill. Env POST_WATCH_NOTICE_BIN. Tests with stub post covering mail/channel/unreadable, hostile strings, over-cap, empty, failure, flag passthrough, no --room pin by default.
acceptance_criteria: node --test skills/post/hooks/watch-notice.test.mjs green. A hostile subject never appears on stdout. Grok monitor can wrap: node <copied-watch-notice> [--once|--snapshot].
close_reason: Shipped watch-notice.mjs plus watch-notice.test.mjs. One metadata-only line per batch; empty snapshot silent exit 0; scan failure UNKNOWN exit 1; Cursor/Grok installers copy it as post-watch-notice.mjs. node --test skills/post/hooks/*.test.mjs 192/192.

title: Cursor CLI lifecycle adapter, installer, and tests

design: Port claude-mail.mjs. EVENTS={sessionStart,beforeSubmitPrompt,postToolUse}. title: Cursor CLI and Grok Build post adapter parity
description:
Bring cursor-agent (Cursor CLI) and grok (Grok Build CLI) up to Claude Code / Codex post-mail parity: activity-gated lifecycle notices plus a safe idle-wake path. post itself already has watch --snapshot/--once; this is adapter, installer, test, and docs work only.

Adapter contract (docs/ADAPTERS.md) is non-negotiable: envelope metadata only, validate-or-UNKNOWN, 20-id/4KiB cap, current-snapshot dedupe, commit-after-delivery, fail-open, no pgrep/pkill.

Do not reuse claude-mail.mjs as-is — stdin/event/output shapes differ. Do not rely on Grok's Claude-compat scan of ~/.claude/settings.json: exec-form args are dropped (target becomes bare node) and SessionStart/PostToolUse stdout is ignored by Grok.

Twin adapters following claude-mail.mjs / codex-mail.mjs (copy with contract deltas, no shared mega-module).

Cursor: sessionStart/beforeSubmitPrompt/postToolUse, additional_context output, room from cwd|workspace_roots[0]|process.cwd().

Grok: UserPromptSubmit only (SessionStart/PostToolUse stdout ignored — committing seen there would hide mail the model never saw).

Native wake: validating watch-notice renderer for Grok monitor and Cursor background --once.

Herdr doorbell already wakes any named agent including cursor/grok; document that, do not fork the Codex installer unless paths become a problem.
acceptance_criteria: node --test skills/post/hooks/*.test.mjs green including new cursor/grok/watch-notice suites; no regressions in claude/codex/doorbell. Installers are hermetic, idempotent, preserve unrelated hooks, require an explicit target path, copy adapters to private hook dirs. Docs (ADAPTERS.md, README, SKILL.md) list both harnesses with install commands and wake caveats.

comments.author: Trey Goff
comments.text:
Phase 0 rulings, decided by the agent per Trey's instruction ('you are an agent, so you decide: which will be best for agents like you using the tool'):
1. Cursor granularity: per-room-per-channel cursors, plus one per-room mail cursor. Agents catch up channel-by-channel; a room-level cursor would mark every channel read after one catchup, and per-message read-marks are write amplification with no catchup value.
2. No rollout compat window for armed doorbells: cursors are new orthogonal state; default watch stays cursor-free. Hard invariant: catchup advancing a cursor must NOT suppress watch rings — cursors drive catchup/unread counts, never the doorbell (ring-until-handled stands, watch.rs:266-273).
3. Retention/expiry: out of scope for Plan B.
4. Body previews in watch lines: already ruled by Trey — yes, capped ~80 chars, sanitized, untrusted-framed.
5. CLI read-time framing (banner diet v0.3 layer) rides into Plan B's contract pass as an open question, not pre-decided.
Work resumes on the devbox; HANDOFF.md at repo root carries the full context.

title: watch: self-echo suppression is per-room, so a multi-room watch rings itself
description: scan_batch suppresses a channel message when parsed.message.from == room, but the caller invokes it once per watched room. A single watch over rooms A and B therefore delivers A's own send to B's scan, ringing the session that wrote it. Cost is a harness wake-up per outbound message, which trains the operator to ignore the doorbell -- and an ignored doorbell is worse than none, since it is armed precisely for the message that matters. Fix: suppress when the sender is ANY room this watch covers, not just the room being scanned. Papercut pc2_0112901a36bdc0c4.
acceptance_criteria: A watch over rooms A and B does not emit a channel message sent by A. Existing single-room suppression test still passes. New test watched red before the fix.
close_reason: Fixed then redesigned. The first fix widened self-echo suppression to every watched room (6cf6f40); three panel reviewers and a live two-room reproduction showed it made any monitor deaf to rooms it watches but does not own. Shipped form is opt-in: watch --own <room> declares identities, default empty, so existing behaviour is unchanged (b9f4405). Contract surfaces updated in CONTRACT.md, README.md, SKILL.md and post schema. Panel reviews in docs/reviews/self-echo-union.
